article_title: Type 1 diabetes mellitus and educational attainment in childhood: a systematic review.
citation: Oakley NJ, Kneale D, Mann M, Hilliar M, Dayan C, Gregory JW, French R. (2020). Type 1 diabetes mellitus and educational attainment in childhood: a systematic review. BMJ Open. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2019-033215
title: Physiological and attendance mechanisms through which childhood T1DM may affect educational attainment
description: The review outlines a mechanistic account of how T1DM may affect attainment: recurrent hypoglycaemia can cause neuroglycopenia and "neuronal injury and subsequent cognitive impairment", while hyperglycaemia with ketoacidosis can damage white matter and impair cerebral functioning; hospital appointments or illness may also affect "attendance and attainment" at critical points in the educational trajectory. The review uses this framework to motivate its primary and secondary outcomes (grades and attendance) and to interpret the pronounced Sports/Athletics effect as possibly reflecting anxiety about hypoglycaemia risk.
requirements: Evidence linking clinical aspects of diabetes management (e.g. HbA1c, glycaemic extremes) to cognitive and educational outcomes
constraints: The review presents these mechanisms as potential pathways from prior literature, not as pathways tested within the review itself
target_learners: children and young people with type 1 diabetes in compulsory schooling
target_learning_goals: educational attainment in high stakes standardised testing at the end of compulsory schooling
examples: The review cites prior reviews (Desrocher and Rovet 2004; Gaudieri et al 2008) associating childhood T1DM with poorer neurocognitive outcomes
